name: FWG World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: FWG's top belt, unified at License to Kill into a World Triple Crown when Duke tha Hammer's win over Viper was combined with the N.I.W.F. Heavyweight and FWG Continental titles under the incoming N.I.W.F. ownership. Brick Wall held it into September 2001, when Viper won it back at WrestleSeries.

name: FWG Continental Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: FWG's secondary heavyweight belt, named in its first FAQ and folded into the new World Triple Crown Championship when the N.I.W.F. took over FWG at License to Kill.

name: FWG World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: FWG's tag championship, held by the N.I.W.F.'s Blast and Psycho Cebo after License to Kill, then by Skull and Hellbound, before Sniper and Inferno won it back in a TLC three-way at WrestleSeries.

name: FWG Deathmatch Championship
epitaph: FWG's hardcore title, won by Darkside from the N.I.W.F.'s Hardcore G at License to Kill, held by Firestarter by early September, and won by Rio Nexan in a four-way brawl through a McDonald's at WrestleSeries.

name: FWG World Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: FWG's cruiserweight title, won by Lance Dewlock from Primo Destruccion on the 20 August 2001 Rampage; Dewlock treated the belt as his own personal showcase into the fall.

name: FWG Television Championship
epitaph: FWG's title for up-and-comers, held by Passion until Sheyda won it in a ladder match at WrestleSeries.
